A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XtraQA/XtraGPT study. All 30 pages of each version, including Appendices A–L, figures, tables and equations, support comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model benchmarks, human evaluations and AI-SCIENTIST assessments of 54 papers before and after revision, with supporting appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark, human-evaluation and paper-scoring results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions train on criterion-guided instruction–revision pairs and generate paragraph revisions conditioned on the instruction, original paragraph and full paper. V2 explains these principles more explicitly without changing the architecture, objective or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The ICLR 2024/XtraQA corpus, six section-level revision tasks and paper-scoring evaluations are retained. The shortened illustrative case does not establish a change in the datasets or task requirements evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 3, 4, 6 and 13 retain the same evaluated comparison models. The GPT-4o case comparison also remains; renaming and rearranging systems in the descriptive Table 1 does not add evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the 5% paper-level holdout of 350 papers and 7,000 pairs, length-controlled judging protocol, human-rating criteria and 54-paper AI-SCIENTIST evaluation. The appendix prompts and Table 11 training hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 Table 8 becomes v2 Table 5 but loses the follow-up introduction-revision question, response and claim of referencing the revised abstract. The HARL case, output-length analysis, uncontrolled win rates and Appendix L scaling analysis remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.4 retains three repetitions for t-tests and the same uncertainty and significance reporting, including the overall-rating increase of 0.65±0.15 with p<0.001. No additional seed or statistical-estimation information appears.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results are unchanged: Table 4 still reports 51.75 for GPT-4o-mini and 55.49 for XtraGPT-14B against the 7B anchor, and overall paper ratings remain 6.08 to 6.73. V2 removes the follow-up introduction response from v1 Table 8, reducing the qualitative result record.

T1.justification: The CPT objective, criterion-conditioned argument and length-controlled win-rate equations retain their substance. V2's explicit input–output mapping restates the previously specified task; it introduces no substantive mathematical assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract's dataset, model and performance claims remain unchanged. V2's conclusion adds the stronger claim that empirical success validates iterative refinement as more trustworthy than autonomous generation; v1 described a foundation for trustworthy writing assistants.

C2.justification: V2 Section 5.2 newly interprets the reused case comparison as demonstrating greater practical applicability than GPT-4o. Section 3.2 also develops the rationale for criteria alignment and context conditioning. Existing domain, iterative-memory and evaluator-reliability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V1's explicit MG0-2.0 model-license statement and ModelGo link disappear. Hardware, prompts and appendix hyperparameters remain. This establishes a loss of licensing documentation, not withdrawal of the models or an actual license change.

R1.justification: The ModelGo reference is removed; the other 88 cited works match despite renumbering and renamed table entries. Table 1 adds an explicit description of iterative human–AI feedback, while Section 2 and Appendix A largely retain their positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 are substantially reorganized from dataset-then-model exposition into Methodology and Instantiation, adding dedicated Problem Formulation and Guiding Principles subsections. The title, introduction and conclusion are revised around this framework-centered narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves before the abstract, Table 1 reorders columns, the criteria and validation tables are separated, and the appendix case becomes a compact main-text table. The ICLR rating plot moves to the appendix. V2 Table 8 also incorrectly captions retained AI-SCIENTIST results as XtraGPT performance.

improvement.justification: V2's Methodology/Instantiation structure clarifies the unchanged approach. However, Table 8 introduces an attribution error, licensing information disappears, and the conclusion strengthens comparative trustworthiness claims without additional validation. These clarity gains and reporting losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
